children: CropLife India has urged the Centre to introduce a five-year Regulatory Data Protection (RDP) regime for crop protection products, arguing that it would encourage companies to bring newer molecules to India and widen the range of pest-control options available to farmers.

The industry body, representing 17 research-driven crop protection companies, said Indian farmers currently have access to about 380 active ingredients (AIs), against around 1,200 available globally. Restrictions on existing pesticides without ensuring availability of better alternatives could hurt farmers, it said in a statement Thursday.

CropLife suggested a two-pronged approach, under which restrictions on existing molecules should be based on established scientific literature and contextual safety, health and efficacy data, while also assessing the likely impact on farmers.

At the same time, it sought five-year protection for regulatory data generated by companies for registering new products in India. Such protection would incentivise investment in studies required under Indian conditions and facilitate faster introduction of newer technologies, it said.

CropLife said several countries already provide regulatory data protection, ranging from six years in China, Indonesia and Malaysia to as much as 10 years in the US, European Union, Canada, Thailand, Brazil and Colombia.

“Factors such as El Nino and climate change are making pest pressures even more dynamic and troublesome for farmers,” said Rahul Dhanuka, Managing Director, Dhanuka Agritech. An RDP framework would facilitate entry of improved technologies and enable evidence-based phasing out of older products, he added.

Mohan Babu Boppana, Vice-Chairman, CropLife India, and COO, Bayer CropScience, said time-bound data protection could encourage innovation and fair competition. Newer molecules, including so-called green molecules, tend to be more selective and require lower application doses, which could reduce their environmental impact, he said.
The association estimated that pests and diseases cause annual crop losses of 10-35 per cent in India, valued at about ₹2 lakh crore.
CropLife also said access to newer crop-protection technologies was becoming important for agricultural exports as markets such as the EU tighten maximum residue limits (MRLs) for pesticides.

Separately, the industry body sought tighter regulation of crop protection products sold through e-commerce platforms, including licensing requirements and digital traceability to curb the sale of unauthorised products.

title: CropLife seeks 5-year data protection to widen farmers’ access to new pesticides
